inputs.text: Pakistan-linked security cases are too serious to be built on suspicion—and too serious to be allowed to collapse through careless investigation. The Punjab and Haryana High Court’s decision to grant regular bail is not an acquittal, but it should be a warning to the authorities: protect the country by gathering solid evidence and presenting a case that can stand up in court. Public confidence depends on institutions doing that hard work, not merely invoking national security.
